sources: Reuters satellite review (EU Sentinel 1/2), Kpler and Vortexa data (reported via xe.today)
fault_line: The blockade works — but whose bill is it: Tehran's, or your fuel bill?

sections.what_happened: Analysis of EU ship-tracking data and satellite imagery shows no crude tankers at Iran's Kharg Island export terminal since late August — the longest hiatus since US-Iran tensions escalated in February. Iran's crude exports fell from nearly 1 million bpd in July to zero by late August; United Against Nuclear Iran reports no crude tankers have left Iran since mid-July. Jask port east of the Strait also shows no tankers. Chinese refiners are hunting alternative crude, pushing prices and freight rates up.
sections.what_verified: Reuters satellite imagery review; Kpler and Vortexa export data; United Against Nuclear Iran tanker tracking
sections.what_disputed: Small-volume/shadow-fleet transshipments off-book cannot be fully ruled out by satellite alone; Jask handles only a small export share
sections.why_matters: Zero. Iran's oil exports have flatlined. The naval blockade is doing exactly what it was built to do — and your fuel pump is where the invoice lands.
